clue.text: Warn clubs in decline to move lots on

indicators.note: in a down answer, going into decline means sliding lower down the word

parts.note: to caution is to warn
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Golf clubs that are losing value are flagged to be sold on.
explanation.walkthrough: The C slips two places down CAUTION. The definition is the verb: to auction is to sell off lots.
explanation.definitionFit: To auction is to sell items by bidding, passing lots on to new owners.

clue.text: Dales village found enthusiastic hosts

indicators.note: the words host the answer, holding it inside them

parts.note: the answer spans the end of found and the start of enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A village in the Yorkshire Dales was eager to entertain visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are a national park in northern England; Dent sits in Dentdale. Arthur Dent is the Hitchhiker's hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Dent is a small village in Dentdale, in the Yorkshire Dales National Park.

clue.text: No more pervasive feeling than in the beginning

parts.note: atmos is a short informal form of atmosphere, a mood that pervades a place

indicators.note: in the beginning means take the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of than is T

explanation.surface: A feeling that is no stronger now than it was at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition takes only 'No more'; the phrase means 'not exceeding'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'At most' sets an upper limit, meaning not exceeding or no greater than.

clue.text: Conclude review you shouldn't have written about private war

indicators.note: the review word is written about the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: to vet something is to review it
to conclude is to end
said on receiving a gift, a form of thanks, which is ta

explanation.surface: Someone told to finish a review they ought never to have written about a personal feud.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal thanks, and 'you shouldn't have' is what one says when thanking for a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud carried on between individuals or families rather than nations.

clue.text: At Monaco, one of F1's people's given up, off the record

parts.note: French is spoken in Monaco, and one in French is un
F1 looks like the letters F and I

indicators.note: in a down answer, given up means written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: laic means of the lay people

explanation.surface: At the Monaco Grand Prix, a Formula One official confides something privately.
explanation.walkthrough: The F1 of Formula One stands for the letters FI, the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said off the record is not formally authorised or acknowledged, so it is unofficial.

clue.text: OS zip with clear edges

parts.note: and means with or plus

indicators.note: the with and clear words form the edges, surrounding the zip letter

parts.note: to rid a place of something is to clear it
zip means nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: An operating system ships a zip-file tool with clean borders.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the computing abbreviation for operating system; Marvin is the Paranoid Android of the Hitchhiker's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Android is Google's operating system for mobile phones.

clue.text: Instrument adjusted to cut sound off?

indicators.note: the adjusted word is set to cut into the other word, so it goes inside it

parts.note: with its sound off, a television is on mute
something adjusted has been set, as a clock is set

explanation.surface: A musician tweaks an instrument so it can be silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: A musette is a small French bagpipe; the question mark hints that 'sound off' is not a command here.
explanation.definitionFit: A musette is a small bellows-blown bagpipe, so it is a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: A little rhyme, an ingenious expression

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A short clever verse described as a witty turn of phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The expression on a face or in words conveys a sense, which is what meaning is.

clue.text: What compels nurse to join

parts.note: EN is the abbreviation for Enrolled Nurse
for can stand for to, as in 'a reason for leaving, a reason to leave'
to cement is to join firmly

explanation.surface: A nurse is made to join a union.
explanation.definitionFit: Enforcement is the act of compelling obedience to a law or rule.

clue.text: Two East End sorts funded by the Tories?

definitions.note: a teasing definition: the government pays for what it owns, though Tories are known for selling such things off

indicators.note: to sort things is to rearrange them into a new order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of Cockney characters bankrolled by the Conservative Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End sorts' reads like Londoners, but 'sorts' is the signal to rearrange TWO EAST END. The question mark flags the irony that a Tory government owning things is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: A state-owned body is paid for by the state, which is run by whichever party is in government.

clue.text: President, Republican, taking over from Democrat

definitions.note: Gerald Ford was a Republican US president

parts.note: to stand in for someone is to take over from them, so the word is for
D is the standard abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A Republican president replacing a Democrat in the White House.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as party politics, but 'Republican' belongs to the definition and the Democrat supplies only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was the 38th US President and a member of the Republican Party.

clue.text: So intimate table seats yet vacant? Thematic solution

indicators.note: the table for two seats the other letters, holding them inside itself

parts.note: a romantic restaurant table is a table for two, giving the words for two

indicators.note: vacant means emptied of its middle, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: with its middle emptied, yet leaves its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cosy table for two that nobody has sat at yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' suggests furniture, but a table for two is the phrase wanted. In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, 42 is the answer to the ultimate question, the theme behind ARTHUR, FORD, MARVIN and others.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty-two is the famous 'Answer to the Ultimate Question of Life' in Douglas Adams's novel, the puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Big shot with hotshot legwear

indicators.note: shot as in shot to pieces, wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity and a high-flyer both wearing fancy boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big shot' reads as a VIP, but 'shot' is the signal to rearrange BIG and HOTSHOT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Thigh boots are long boots reaching up the thigh, so they are worn on the legs.

clue.text: Woman phased out in TARDIS climax

indicators.note: letters taken out in phases, on and off, means every other letter

parts.note: the odd letters of these words are kept

explanation.surface: A female companion is written out at the end of a Doctor Who episode inside the time machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the Doctor Who time machine. Tricia McMillan is Trillian's Earth name in the Hitchhiker's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricia is a female given name, short for Patricia.

clue.text: Old doctor's in shot, tending queasy actor

parts.note: in, meaning fashionable, is hip

indicators.note: to tend is to look after, so the shot holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a photographic shot is a pic

indicators.note: feeling queasy, the word is churned into a new order

explanation.surface: An old medic is caught on camera, caring for a sick performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is possessive: the answer means 'of Hippocrates', the Greek physician whose oath doctors still invoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocratic means belonging to Hippocrates, the ancient Greek physician, so it fits a possessive for an old doctor.

clue.text: Suspicious one boxed by Pandora, perhaps?

indicators.note: being boxed by something is to be enclosed in it
perhaps suggests a possible rearrangement of the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Pandora, of the box, shut someone suspicious inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Pandora's box, from Greek myth, is the joke behind 'boxed'. The rearranged PANDORA gives PARANOD, with I inside. Marvin is the Paranoid Android.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone paranoid is unreasonably suspicious and mistrustful of others.

clue.text: Games on court umpire's got on monitor?

indicators.note: to get on a bus is to board it, going inside

parts.note: PE is physical education, school games
a referee, or ref, is an umpire

explanation.surface: School games on the court with an umpire boarding the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A prefect is a senior British school pupil given authority over others; the question mark signals that a monitor is a pupil, not a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A school monitor is a pupil with supervisory duties, much the role of a prefect.

clue.text: Any number admitted to top pub? Quite!

indicators.note: being let into the pub, the letter goes inside

parts.note: the best pub of all is bar one, number one bar
n stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Anyone at all let into the best pub? Absolutely!
explanation.definitionFit: Bar none means without exception, an emphatic agreement like 'absolutely'.

clue.text: King in retreat, at last, for a day

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes backwards, so these letters are turned round
at last points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of for is R
THUR is a short form of Thursday

explanation.surface: A monarch withdrawing, finally, for just a day.
explanation.walkthrough: R and A, turned round, give AR before THUR. Arthur Dent is the hero of the Hitchhiker's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur was the legendary British king of Camelot and the Round Table.

clue.text: 1900 wrongfully assigned to a North Yorkshire poet

parts.note: MCM is 1900 in Roman numerals
ill, as in ill-gotten, means wrongly
N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A date mistakenly given to a poet from the north of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Yorkshire' looks like the county, but North gives only N; Ian McMillan is a Barnsley poet, and Tricia McMillan is Trillian in the Hitchhiker's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian McMillan is a well-known poet and broadcaster from Yorkshire, nicknamed the Bard of Barnsley.

clue.text: Newer Bible in the charge of principal boy

indicators.note: being in someone's charge is being held by them, so it goes inside

parts.note: principal means main
RV is the Revised Version, a later Bible translation

explanation.surface: A newer Bible is entrusted to the leading man of a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal boy' looks like the pantomime hero role, but 'boy' alone is the definition. Marvin is the Paranoid Android.
explanation.definitionFit: Marvin is a male first name, so it names a boy.

clue.text: In which event is female entering ring?

indicators.note: the female letter goes into the word is

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman is stepping into the boxing ring at some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'event' suggests a sports event, but the definition is a conditional phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: 'If so' means 'if that is the case', the same conditional sense as 'in which event'.

clue.text: Niger's wingers see back taking a performance-enhancer

parts.note: the outer letters of Niger are N and R, written out as N AND R

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look
a means one

explanation.surface: A Nigerian footballer's wide players being caught out by a doping test.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'wingers' of Niger are N and R, taken as the words N AND R. Nandrolone is an anabolic steroid banned in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Nandrolone is an anabolic steroid that athletes have taken illegally to build strength.

clue.text: What's it all about, Alfie? Topless dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order
a topless word has its head, its first letter, removed

explanation.surface: Michael Caine's Alfie strips off and dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's it all about, Alfie?' is the opening line of the song from the 1966 film Alfie, and the answer to what it is all about is the meaning of existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Life is what the question 'what's it all about?' is traditionally asking about, as in the meaning of life.

clue.text: Duplex Viz gags excessive for Barker

indicators.note: to gag is to put something in the mouth, so the outer letters hold the others

parts.note: viz, meaning namely, is given in two forms: SC for scilicet and IE for id est
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: The comic magazine Viz goes too far with its jokes, by the standards of a comedian named Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: Viz is also a British comic famous for crude jokes, and Ronnie Barker was a comedian; here a Barker is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is a Scottish terrier, and a barker is a dog.

clue.text: Glassmaker spat some

parts.note: a spat is a small quarrel, a tiff
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A glassmaker spat some out.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Comfort Tiffany was the American designer famous for stained glass lamps and windows.
